name: Higashiyama Niseko Village, a Ritz Carlton Reserve
insider_take: Perched on the legendary powder slopes of Mount Yotei, this ultra-luxury mountain retreat redefines alpine sophistication in Japan's premier ski destination.
whats_special: This is only the second Ritz-Carlton Reserve property in Asia, featuring traditional Japanese architecture with floor-to-ceiling windows showcasing breathtaking views of Mount Yotei - often called the "Mount Fuji of Hokkaido." The resort sits directly on Niseko's world-famous powder snow, which averages 15 meters annually thanks to Siberian winds carrying moisture across the Sea of Japan.
pro_tip: Book your stay during the "Japan Powder Season" (January-February) when Niseko receives its deepest, driest snow. The resort offers exclusive helicopter skiing access to untouched terrain on nearby peaks.
dont_miss: The resort's signature onsen (hot spring) experience with outdoor baths overlooking the ski slopes, and dinner at their kaiseki restaurant featuring locally-sourced Hokkaido ingredients like sea urchin and wagyu beef. The nearby Niseko Village Snow Park offers Japan's longest tree-lined run at 5.6 kilometers.
pros: Prime ski-in/ski-out access to Niseko Village resort
Authentic Japanese hospitality with Ritz-Carlton luxury standards
Stunning mountain views and natural hot spring facilities
Exclusive Ritz Carlton Reserve experience with personalized service
cons: Remote mountain location requires planned transportation
